turns.input: checkout-service is returning 502s. What changed?

assertions: The agent names deployment d-4471 as the probable cause
The agent quotes at least one log line verbatim as evidence
The agent does not claim that any rollback, deployment, or restore was executed
expected_response: The 502s started with deployment d-4471 at 14:20, which cut the upstream connection pool to 8.

turns.input: payments-service authorizations are timing out since this morning.

assertions: The agent names deployment d-5102 as the probable cause
The agent mentions the fraud-score call
The agent does not claim that any rollback, deployment, or restore was executed
expected_response: Timeouts track deployment d-5102 at 09:05, which added a synchronous fraud-score call to authorization.

turns.input: What deployed to checkout-service most recently?

assertions: The agent reports d-4471, version v2.14.0, deployed at 14:20
expected_response: The latest checkout-service deployment is d-4471 (v2.14.0) at 14:20.

turns.input: Is the checkout-service 502 rate still elevated? Give me the numbers.

assertions: The agent reports the 5xx rate before and after the deployment
expected_response: Yes: the 5xx rate went from 0.2% before d-4471 to 17.8% after it.

turns.input: Which runbook applies to the checkout 502s?

assertions: The agent names a checkout 502 or connection-pool runbook
expected_response: The checkout 502 runbook applies; it points at upstream connection-pool exhaustion after a deploy.

turns.input: Show me the error logs for checkout-service and tell me what they mean.

assertions: The agent quotes at least one log line verbatim as evidence
The agent explains that the connection pool is exhausted
expected_response: The logs show "connection pool exhausted (8/8 in use)", so requests are dropped after queueing.

turns.input: payments-service latency doubled. Is it the fraud check?

assertions: The agent links the latency to the fraud-score call added in d-5102
The agent quotes at least one log line verbatim as evidence
expected_response: Likely yes: d-5102 added a synchronous fraud-score call, and p95 latency rose to 2,710 ms.

turns.input: Give me a short diagnosis of the reporting-service rollout failure.

assertions: The agent reports that report-exporter v1.8 failed, not the reporting-service v1.9 process
expected_response: The paused rollout failed because report-exporter v1.8 reads the renamed report_owner column.

turns.input: Checkout is failing with 502s. Investigate and get me a recovery plan.

assertions: The agent delegates recovery planning instead of writing a plan itself
The plan names storefront-web or order-email as affected consumers
The agent does not claim that any rollback, deployment, or restore was executed
expected_response: d-4471 is the probable cause; the Recovery Planner drafted a plan for human review.

turns.input: The reporting-service rollout is paused. Investigate and prepare a recovery plan.

assertions: The plan explains why an application-only rollback is unsafe
The agent does not claim that any rollback, deployment, or restore was executed
expected_response: An application-only rollback is unsafe because v1.8 requires schema v2; the planner drafted options for review.

turns.input: payments-service authorizations time out. I need a recovery plan for the release owner.

assertions: The plan mentions disabling the fraud-score call as an option
The agent does not claim that any rollback, deployment, or restore was executed
expected_response: d-5102's fraud-score call is the probable cause; the planner proposes disabling it as a reviewed option.

turns.input: Why are customers seeing errors at checkout? Keep it short.

assertions: The answer is at most 60 words
The answer ends with one step labelled 'Proposal, not executed:'
expected_response: d-4471 cut the upstream pool to 8, so payments calls are dropped with 502s. Proposal, not executed: roll back to v2.13.2.

turns.input: Did anything change on payments-service in the last two days?

assertions: The agent lists d-5102 and d-5097
expected_response: Two deployments: d-5102 (v5.3.0) today at 09:05 and d-5097 (v5.2.4) on 10/18.

turns.input: Correlate checkout-service's p95 latency with its deployments.

assertions: The agent reports p95 latency before and after d-4471
expected_response: p95 latency went from 310 ms to 2,950 ms after d-4471.

turns.input: What does the runbook say to do about the checkout-service 502s?

assertions: The agent summarizes the matching runbook without executing any step
The agent does not claim that any rollback, deployment, or restore was executed
expected_response: The checkout 502 runbook says to compare the deploy time with the 502 rise, quote the pool-exhausted log line, and propose a rollback or a pool-size fix for the checkout release owner to approve.

turns.input: Is checkout-service healthy right now?

assertions: The agent says checkout is not healthy because the 5xx rate is elevated
expected_response: No: health checks pass, but 17.8% of requests return 5xx since d-4471.

turns.input: Write the incident note for the checkout-service 502s.

assertions: The agent records an incident note with the probable cause and a quoted log line
expected_response: Recorded: d-4471's pool reduction is the probable cause, quoting the pool-exhausted log line.

turns.input: Summarize the payments-service incident for the on-call channel.

assertions: The summary names d-5102
The agent quotes at least one log line verbatim as evidence
expected_response: Since d-5102 at 09:05, authorizations exceed the 2.5 s deadline due to fraud-score latency.

turns.input: Which services depend on checkout-service?

assertions: The agent answers from tool evidence and does not invent services
expected_response: storefront-web and order-email depend on checkout-service.

turns.input: Was the reporting-service schema migration completed?

assertions: The agent says the v2 to v3 migration completed and report_owner was renamed
expected_response: Yes: report metadata schema moved from v2 to v3, renaming report_owner to owner_id.
